_README: Documented suppressions for the pixel-art QA checks.
A validator that reports 278 findings of which most are false is worse than no
validator, because the next person learns to ignore it. Every entry here is a
case where the check's assumption does not hold for that sprite, with the reason
and the evidence. Suppressing a finding requires naming the line of engine code
that makes the check inapplicable — if you cannot, it is a real defect.
Add to 'sprites' to silence specific codes for one sprite.
Add to 'shadowed_by_override' to declare that a store's copy of a sprite never
renders because a later store overrides it.
Sprites the engine draws CENTRED rather than from the top-left. For these,
frames of differing size are legitimate — the art grows symmetrically about
the centre — so E1 and A1 do not apply.

centre.inv_bolt: runtime.ts:1997 drawSpr(x,img,b.x-img.width/2,b.y-img.height/2) — and the afterglow at :1995 uses the same centre. The 5x5/5x7/5x9/5x7 frame ladder is a deliberate throb that pulses outward from a fixed core.

_README: eggPx6() at runtime.ts:5254 replaces SPR/SPRF/SPRW for every key present in
EART6. Where a name exists in both stores the EGG_ART copy never reaches the
screen, so its palette and readability numbers describe art that is not shown.
Report the EART6 figure as the live one.

inv_bolt.reason: Centre-drawn: see anchors.centre. The frame-size ladder is the animation, not a defect.

capsule.reason: Composited, not standalone. The capsule is a window frame and the engine draws a pk_* icon inside it at x+1,y+1 (docblock at runtime.ts:2871), so the dark interior is the aperture the icon shows through. Contrast has to be measured on the composite, which the checks do not model.

explosion.reason: An expanding effect. Bounding-box growth and a swing in opaque pixel count are what an explosion IS; the foot-slide and crop-error checks assume a body with feet.

dust.reason: Same as explosion: a dissipating particle puff.

player_death.reason: A dissolve, per the docblock at runtime.ts:2865. The silhouette is meant to break up.

_README: Recorded so they are not silently re-suppressed later. These are open, not excused.
known_real_defects.e_bulb@EART6: The 16-bit pass narrowed its luminance spread from 1.000 to 0.801. e_bulb is a light source; it should hold the widest spread in its zone, not a narrower one. Regression introduced by the pass, not inherited.
known_real_defects.e_moth@EART6: Lost a colour in the 16-bit pass, 5 -> 4. Only sprite of the 82 to regress on colour count.
known_real_defects.e_p_down/e_p_side/e_p_up@EART6: Four-frame walk cycles with only three unique frames (f0 == f2). Costs nine redundant compiled canvases at init. Harmless to rendering, wasteful, and it means the walk has a hitch rather than a true 4-beat cycle. Changing the frame count touches animation timing, so it needs a gameplay decision before it is fixed.
known_real_defects.e_d_floor: Best colour in the tile reaches only 1.60:1 on the void. Same class of defect as the cave floor fixed on 12 Aug 2026 — the dungeon floor is the next one to redraw.
